l.i: Quomodo λόγῳ[?] sit in suo templo, hoc est corpore.
TERTIA demonstrat, ad controuersiam de cœna Domini non pertinere disputationē de potentia Dei, eiusq; uerbi ueritate: deq; isto non admetiendo ad rationis regulam.
Obiter notat ἀταξίαν[?], quam D. Tilemannus suo exemplo in Ecclesiam inducit.
IN QVARTA, recitantur & refutantur illustres calumniæ, quibus D. Tilemannus aduersarios iniuste grauat, & ipsorum sententiam odiosam reddere conatur.
Additur Coronis, continens orationis Tilemannica lumina, hoc est conuicia, quibus uelut gemmis ornare, & flosculis uariare orationem suam assolet.

page.notes: The pilcrow marks (¶) in the left margin are printed paragraph signs, transcribed as notes. The first Greek word, after "Quomodo", is set as λόγῳ with the dative ending; it is in a cursive-looking form and the accent or iota subscript is doubtful. The Greek word ἀταξίαν is doubtful in its accents. The small superscript marks after "eiusq;" and "deq;" are hard to read and may be reference signs or numerals; they have no matching note on this page. "Tilemannica" runs over a line end at "Tileman / nica" with no printed hyphen visible, so it is written whole. Catchword "D. TILE-" is right-aligned below the text.
